title: Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon — visual production catalogue
status: Depiction and atlas plan; no artwork acceptance implied.

source.design_data_read: runs/cosmic/design-data.json; scratch inventory consulted, final names and recipe modes refreshed from manuscript

style.medium: Original hand-tinted astronomical chromolithograph with chalk and dry-gouache masses, feathered light edges, sparse stipple and broad legible silhouettes.

palette.rock_and_metal: charcoal basalt, subdued copper-gray mineral facets
palette.ice: translucent pale ivory with a faint cool cast

presentation.ground: opaque indigo inside one thin pale ring, true alpha transparency outside
presentation.subject_margin: Entire subject stays within ring; dark breathing room, no external shadow. Export circle nearly fills the common 288px square.
presentation.labels: No letters, numbers, formulas, captions, cell IDs or grid lines in artwork.

reference.scope: Technique and atmosphere only: swept feathered ivory light, irregular rays, subtle grain and large quiet dark fields. Not copied subjects or scientific models.

conventions: Atom and molecule views use diffuse electron clouds with schematic nuclear centres; never misleading planetary electron orbits.
Forces, flow and energy transfer may use at most a few broad pictorial directional cues; no hardware, observers or hands.
Keep the same substance appearance across distinct histories. Exact chemistry, temperature and invisible physical conditions can require normal names and readings.
Cutaways clearly belong to one body. No equal-scale claim across particles, grains, stars, worlds and landscape views.
Do not manufacture visible chemistry by adding diagnostic colours, salt crystals to dissolved water or water droplets to hydrated rock.
All coast scenes use one stepped basalt headland on the left, a low inland ridge on the right and the sheltered basin between, camera facing across the basin.
Earth retains an orange molten interior and cracked charcoal basalt through hot stages; later Earth is bare rock and teal water, never vegetation or modern continents.
Early Moon stays pale gray/ivory after cooling, with sparse subtle relief and no familiar dark maria. No compulsory modern crater map.
No modern machinery, instruments, hands, people, buildings, biological soil, plants, animals, shells, algae, intentional faces, glossy lens flares or decorative star fields on Earth.

recognition_limits.target: Recognize subject family and neighboring physical state at 72px with normal item labels and readings available.
recognition_limits.not_claimed: No blind exact-chemistry recognition, quantitative scale, unique planetary history or empirical human preference established by this plan.
review_priorities: At 72px compare neutral atoms with bare nuclei, gas with solids, dust mantles with bare grains, nested shell interiors with Earth core, scattered versus falling debris.
Compare same-body states together: Earth, Moon, giant star, asteroid, grain-surface chemistry and repeated coastal geometry.
Distinguish clear dissolved load from visibly suspended sediment; hot clear hydrothermal fluid from precipitated mineral plume.
Compare directional processes in opposite directions: collapse/escape, descending/rising fluid, flooding/draining shore.
Use label-supported checks for chemically identical-looking states; do not repair ambiguity by inventing false colours.
